### 1. What the customer expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Object, timing, boundary and authorisation are all expressed plainly: "I collect the car tomorrow and I want to know what the cover on this trip is going to cost me and have it charged before I pick it up", with the observation that "the trip itself has been charged to her card, there is a delivery charge and a marketplace fee, and there is nothing at all against the protection"; and "She is happy for the desk to do whatever it can from where it sits, and if some part of it can only come from her she will do it there and then rather than be called back."

Identification is elicited one item at a time: mobile `7372208456`, then DOB `1996-11-03`, licence `53627105`, postal code `78702`, email `rosalind.ueda@northloopmail.com`, "one at a time and only on being asked". She holds no internal reference: "the app only shows her the trip, not the numbers behind it, and asks the agent to pull it up their end". She will not name a price: "she has no idea and would rather not guess".

Three facts she will confirm on being asked are load-bearing below: "the car is coming to her hotel rather than being collected", "the residency runs to the middle of August", "she has rented from the same host three or four times before"; plus two negatives — "she does not run a car of her own and has nothing in her own name", and asked whether anyone else will be driving, "no, it is just her".

The simulator is passive. It states the need once, answers what it is asked, reacts conditionally ("If the agent comes back and tells her that the protection on this trip is still only a quote, that the marketplace cannot take the choice on her behalf, and which level is the one open to her and how many days of cover it would run for…") and executes the owner=user tool only on hand-over ("when the step is handed over to her she takes it herself there and then").

#### (a) The level open to her — **Keyturn Advantage Protection**, and it is unique

Three visible schedules intersect to a single level.
- `driver_admission_terms_b41d9e05`, minimum marketplace driver score: Declined 80, Minimum 68, Standard 70, Advantage 72, Premier 74, Business Traveler 76. Her `driver_score=73` shuts out Premier, Business Traveler and Declined. `election_eligibility_terms_0b9e34c7`: "A level … is open to a guest only where the guest meets its minimum driver age and its minimum marketplace driver score on the day the trip starts". Her age on 2026-06-02 is 29 whole years, which clears every level's minimum.
- `vehicle_and_trip_limits_9a2ce7f4`, value ceiling: Minimum 85000.00 USD — the vehicle is valued at 92000.00 USD, so Minimum is shut out. Standard's ceiling is 120000.00 and Advantage's 175000.00; the Keyturn Luxury Class Listing appears on the excluded-class list of Declined alone, so class shuts out nothing further here.
- Same table, "Longest trip covered (whole days)": Standard 60, Advantage 90. `claim_history_and_days_read_together_41fc9a0b`: "a guest whose covered days would take one trip past the level's maximum trip length is quoted on the level that will carry the whole trip rather than on one that would run out midway", restated as "Length is quoted forward, not discovered later." The days of cover come to 81 (below), and the reserved period itself is 75 days; both exceed Standard's 60. Standard is therefore out.

What survives: **Keyturn Advantage Protection** alone. The persona's script expects exactly this shape — "which level is the one open to her" — and her own count of days already covered in the calendar year is nil (`find_guestplan_charges` returns nothing), so that half of the same rule adds nothing.

The minimum cover days are 1. The cover ceiling is 30 days", and an explicit order: divide and carry up, then raise to the minimum, then hold down to the ceiling.

| `handover_grace_on_an_election_f70b53a1` | "Delivered to the guest anywhere else → 1 day", the document naming a hotel expressly: "a delivery to a home address, an office or a hotel is a delivery anywhere else and carries 1 day" | booking `pickup_channel='delivery'`, `delivery_location_type='hotel'`; corroborated by the persona, "the car is coming to her hotel rather than being collected" |

- reserved period 2026-06-02 → 2026-08-15 = 29 + 31 + 15 = **75 days** (and 1800 ÷ 24 = 75, so the two readings of "the reserved period" agree)
- whole weeks: 75 = ten whole weeks and a part week → eleven weeks → **77 plan days**
- + 3 late cover days + 1 day of handover grace = **81**
- raised to the minimum of 1: no effect; held under the ceiling of 120: no effect

The election's own `coverage_days=75` is not taken: it stands on a `quoted` election, and `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77` makes the fixing of the days part of the settling itself — "At that moment the marketplace also fixes how many days of cover the election will carry, so that the guest is told which day cover ends on rather than discovering it at a claim."

#### (c) The protection fee — **3272.03 USD**, with a recorded ordering ambiguity

Baseline, `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa`: "The charged days are the election's covered days, never fewer than the level's minimum charge days"; "The protection fee for a trip is the level's daily amount for the charged days, held at the level's floor and then under the ceiling on the protection fee for one trip, which is 1200.00 USD, and rounded to two decimal places only once the whole of it has been worked out." Advantage's row: daily amount 38.00 USD, floor 38.00 USD, minimum charge days 1. Charged days = 81.

|---|---|---|

| `ceiling_on_the_protection_fee_for_one_trip_c7196e3f` | "2 or more whole months → 3200.00 USD" | reserved period 2026-06-02 → 2026-08-15: 6/2→7/2 and 7/2→8/2 are two whole months, 8/2→9/2 falls past the last reserved day |
| `long_stay_discount_on_the_protection_fee_3b84cc17` | "60 days or more → 12.0 percent" | reserved period of 75 days |
| `loyalty_rate_on_the_protection_fee_9f2071ab` | "2 trips or more … and no mileage overage charged in that time → 0.95" | three base-rate-charged trips inside the window (2026-05-20, 2026-01-02, 2025-09-08); the only mileage overage, 2025-04-13, falls outside it. The tier is robust: dropping the present trip from the count still leaves 2 |
| `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2` | "3000 miles or more → 90.00 USD", and "The step is added after the fee has been held at the level's floor and under its ceiling, and the step itself is not held down by that ceiling" | booking `included_miles_total=7500` |

- trip price = 145.00 × 75 reserved days = **10875.00 USD** (`basis_…`: "the daily rate locked in on the trip taken for each of the reserved days")
- daily basis = 38.00 × 81 = 3078.00; share basis = 35 % × 10875.00 = 3806.25; greater = **3806.25**
- less the long-stay discount 12.0 % → 3349.50; at the loyalty rate 0.95 → **3182.025**
- floor 38.00: no effect. Ceiling 3200.00: 3182.025 stands below it, so "the ceiling does not touch it"
- + mileage step 90.00 = 3272.025
- **= 3272.03 USD**, rounded at the end.

**Ambiguity recorded, and it is material here.** Where the long-stay discount and the loyalty rate stand relative to the floor/ceiling clamp is not stated anywhere in the corpus. The baseline document gives an explicit order that contains neither of them ("The charged days are settled first… The level's daily amount is then taken… The figure so reached is raised to the level's floor if it stands below it, and only then held down to 1200.00 USD"). The mileage-step document pins its own position ("after the fee has been held at the level's floor and under its ceiling"); the discount and loyalty documents pin nothing, saying only that the discount "is taken off the protection fee" and that the loyalty rate "is the share of the protection fee a guest … is asked for".
- Reading A, adopted above — the discount and the loyalty rate are taken on the fee as it is built, and the clamp then applies to the fee so built. Two things favour it: the mileage document troubles to say its step "is not held down by that ceiling", which is informative only if the other adjustments are inside the clamp; and applying a reduction after the floor would let the fee fall below the floor the level records, defeating it. Result **3272.03 USD**.
- Reading B — the clamp applies to the fee the baseline produces, and the two multipliers are then taken on the capped figure: 3806.25 → 3200.00 → × 0.88 × 0.95 = 2675.20 → + 90.00 = **2765.20 USD**.
The two readings differ by 506.83 USD. Both are honest readings of the visible sentences; I could find no sentence in any of the 51 documents that closes the boundary. This is carried forward as the principal candidate defect of this task.

A second, smaller gap: the rounding mode is never named — "rounded to two decimal places" only — and 3182.025 + 90.00 = 3272.025 lands exactly on a half-cent, so half-up gives 3272.03 and half-even 3272.02. I take half-up and record the gap.

A third, cosmetic one: `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2` writes "held at the level's floor and under **its** ceiling", whose possessive points at the level, while the ceiling actually in force is the one the baseline names, "the ceiling on the protection fee for one trip". `protection_fee_schedule_7c1a4b93` does record a per-level "Ceiling recorded" column (2400.00 USD for Advantage), and `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150` retires the clause that applied it — "The fee arrived at is then held between the level's floor and its ceiling, the floor applied first and the ceiling last…" — "no longer in force". So the retired reading is closed by the corpus, but the mileage document's pronoun still points at it. Under either referent the position of the step is the same and 3272.03 is unaffected.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer named one problem: charge the protection fee. The visible materials yield two.

**Problem B (root, the one she named) — charge the protection fee for the trip.**
Hop B→A, **state-derived**. `charging_the_protection_fee_ae52c3d9` states, in the hub of the blocked problem: *"The protection fee for a trip is fixed only once the election has left the quoted state and carries the number of days of cover the level will run for."* A state form with the ordering connective "only once"; it names no tool but its own, no other policy, and no route. Checking the state: `find_guestplan_elections(customer_id=…)` returns `status='quoted'`. The waited-on state plainly fails. Searching the corpus with the sentence's own words — "quoted", "the days of cover the level will run for" — reaches `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77`, which describes the write that brings it about: "A Keyturn Guest Protection Plan election is settled when the guest takes the level that will cover their trip. At that moment the marketplace also fixes how many days of cover the election will carry… the quote on it is no longer a quote." Corroborated independently by `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150`: "A fee line is posted only while the election is in the elected or active state, since a quote that was never chosen is never charged", and "The elected state and the active state both admit a fee line; a quote that was never chosen does not." That is Problem A.

**Problem A — settle the level and the days of cover.**
No prerequisite sentence stands in `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77`; its own conditions are met (item 2); and it is the guest's own write, which the persona performs on being handed the tool.

**Direction and handling order:** A → B. Both hops **state-derived**; neither is action-named and **neither is pre-solved**. A scan of all 51 documents for the `name_xxxxxxxx` tool pattern shows each of the five tool identifiers occurring in exactly one document, its own hub; no document names another problem's tool, states a route, or aggregates the chain.

The second half of the derivation — that the level must move from Keyturn Standard Protection to Keyturn Advantage Protection, and that the days come to 81 rather than the 75 standing on the quote — is not a prerequisite hop but is equally unstated by the customer, and it too is reached only by reading schedules against records (item 4(a), 4(b)).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The visible materials fully support the conclusion reached**, subject to the one ordering ambiguity recorded at 4(c). Every other figure traces to a document sentence and a query return named above.

**The closest alternative at each boundary the source itself closes, and what closes it:**
- *Charge the fee now, on the quote.* Closed by the prerequisite sentence in `charging_the_protection_fee_ae52c3d9` read against `status='quoted'`, and independently by `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150`'s state clause.
- *Settle the level on her behalf.* Closed by `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77`: "Only the guest decides what their own cover will be, so the marketplace does not settle a level on their behalf", and by the tool's owner.
- *Keep Keyturn Standard Protection, the level on the quote.* Closed by `vehicle_and_trip_limits_9a2ce7f4` (Standard's longest trip covered is 60 whole days against a 75-day reserved period and 81 days of cover) together with `claim_history_and_days_read_together_41fc9a0b` ("quoted on the level that will carry the whole trip rather than on one that would run out midway").
- *Go higher than Advantage.* Closed by `driver_admission_terms_b41d9e05`: Premier requires a minimum marketplace driver score of 74 and Business Traveler 76, against her 73. Advantage's 72 is the highest she meets. The level is therefore unique, not merely the cheapest adequate one.
- *Take Keyturn Declined Protection since she says she has no cover of her own.* Closed twice: `election_eligibility_terms_0b9e34c7` requires evidence of the guest's own motor policy on the election record, which is empty; and Declined's minimum score of 80 exceeds hers.
- *Take Keyturn Minimum Protection as the cheapest.* Closed by `vehicle_and_trip_limits_9a2ce7f4`: its value ceiling is 85000.00 USD against a vehicle valued at 92000.00 USD.
- *Take the 75 days standing on the election.* Closed by `settling_protection_for_a_trip_0c48ea77` (the days are fixed at settling) and by the measure in `days_of_cover_an_election_carries_b6d1f28c` as varied by the three factors at 4(b).
- *Treat the delivery as a collection.* Closed by `handover_grace_on_an_election_f70b53a1`: "A collection is not a delivery"; the booking records `pickup_channel='delivery'`, `delivery_location_type='hotel'`, and the document names a hotel expressly.
- *Count her April 2025 mileage overage into the loyalty rate.* Closed by the window definition read against the 2026-06-01 handling date.
- *Where the source leaves a boundary open, the documents leave it open too:* the position of the discount and the loyalty rate relative to the clamp, and the rounding mode. Both are recorded at 4(c) as open; I do not close either.

**Counter-proof against the natural wrong answer "she asked for one thing, so do one thing".** Posting the fee alone is excluded by reasoning: `charging_the_protection_fee_ae52c3d9` says the fee "is fixed only once the election has left the quoted state and carries the number of days of cover the level will run for"; the election stands `quoted` with no days the level will run for fixed; so a fee posted now would be fixed on a state the principle does not admit — and `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150` confirms that "a quote that was never chosen" does not admit a fee line at all. Both sentences are record-visible states, and the resolving write is found from the depended-on documents, not handed over. No hop is pre-solved.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.** Reading only the baseline computation documents and the figures they name:
- days of cover, baseline only (`days_of_cover_an_election_carries_b6d1f28c`): 1800 ÷ 24 = 75, carried up = 75, above the minimum of 1, held down to the cover ceiling of 30 → **30 days**, definite;
- the protection fee, baseline only (`protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa` at those 30 charged days on Advantage): 38.00 × 30 = 1140.00, above the floor of 38.00 and below 1200.00 → **1140.00 USD**, definite.
Both are computable from the computation document plus the figures it names, and both differ from the answers reached (81 days, 3272.03 USD), so every declared ladder bears weight on this world.

**Findability of each factor document from the customer's own records:**
- `plan_days_metered_by_rate_plan_…` — the booking's `rate_plan_name`, "the rate plan the trip is priced under";
- `late_return_allowance_on_cover_…` — the ledger rows the records call a late return charged;
- `handover_grace_on_an_election_…` — the booking's delivery, "as the delivery recorded on the Keyturn Trip Booking shows it";
- `cover_ceiling_by_reserved_time_…` — the booking's reserved hours;
- `basis_the_protection_fee_is_arrived_at_on_…` — the level's charging basis and the locked-in daily rate;
- `ceiling_on_the_protection_fee_for_one_trip_…` and `long_stay_discount_…` — the trip's start and end dates, in whole months and in days;
- `loyalty_rate_on_the_protection_fee_…` — the ledger rows for a base rate charged and a mileage overage charged;
- `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_…` — the booking's included miles.
Each was reached from a record, not from the computation document's wording. Neither `days_of_cover_an_election_carries_b6d1f28c` nor `protection_fee_for_a_trip_1c6d80fa` hints that any variation exists: no "unless", no "adjustments may apply", no exception list, no pointer, no statement that certain customers qualify for something else.

**On the two authoring choices flagged for testing.** (i) The prerequisite sentence homed verbatim in the blocked problem's hub rather than in a fragment: in this task it worked as intended — the hub `charging_the_protection_fee_ae52c3d9` is the document any solver handling "charge the protection fee" must read, it is titled for its general subject, and the sentence sits in it before the invocation block, so the hop was discoverable without a search for it. (ii) The wording "the ceiling on the protection fee for one trip" / "the cover ceiling": in both computation documents the phrase is attached to a figure in the same sentence ("the ceiling on the protection fee for one trip, which is 1200.00 USD"; "The cover ceiling is 30 days"), so each names a definite quantity and each baseline yields a definite number. I judge the wording adequate on that test and record no indefiniteness. It does, however, leave a collision: `protection_fee_schedule_7c1a4b93` carries a per-level "Ceiling recorded" column, so the corpus holds two things a reader may call a ceiling on the protection fee. The collision is resolved — `protection_fee_charging_basis_e92b7150` retires the clause that applied the level's recorded ceiling — except in `mileage_exposure_step_on_the_fee_6ad0f4b2`, whose "under **its** ceiling" points at the retired one. Recorded at 4(c).

### Every scored argument matches, but the match rested on a reading the corpus does not close

The blind derivation reached the source's number on every scored value. - **2490.00** — clamp at the level's *recorded* ceiling of 2400.00, which two documents still present as governing (see the bijection report, findings B1 and B2), plus 90.00.

Only the first is right, and nothing a solver can read says so. That is a bijection failure, recorded as **KB-BIJECTION RED** in `policy_kb/guest_protection_desk/1.md`, findings B1–B3.
